### shield-auto-l7-managed-rule-group

**Claim.** In Shield Advanced automatic application layer DDoS mitigation (the legacy Layer 7 Auto Mitigation, superseded by the Anti-DDoS Managed Rule Group), when automatic mitigation is enabled for a resource, Shield Advanced maintains a rule group in the resource's associated web ACL with a rate-based rule for known DDoS sources, compares current traffic patterns against historic traffic baselines, and responds to detected attacks by deploying additional, custom AWS WAF rules in the rule group.

**Write it as.** `rule group in the resource's associated web ACL` · `compares current traffic patterns against historic traffic baselines`

**Scope.** per Shield Advanced protected resource; automatic mitigation enabled; legacy feature: new Shield Advanced customers need AWS Support to access it.

> "When automatic mitigation is enabled for a resource, Shield Advanced maintains a rule group in the resource's associated web ACL where it manages mitigation rules on behalf of the resource. The rule group contains a rate-based rule that tracks the volume of requests from IP addresses that are known to be sources of DDoS attacks."
> — [Automating application layer DDoS mitigation with Shield Advanced](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-automatic-app-layer-response.html)

> "Additionally, Shield Advanced compares current traffic patterns against historic traffic baselines to detect deviations that might indicate a DDoS attack. Shield Advanced responds to detected DDoS attacks by creating, evaluating, and deploying additional, custom AWS WAF rules in the rule group."
> — [Automating application layer DDoS mitigation with Shield Advanced](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-automatic-app-layer-response.html)

> "It supersedes the Layer 7 Auto Mitigation (L7AM) feature."
> — [Automating application layer DDoS mitigation with Shield Advanced](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-automatic-app-layer-response.html)

> "If you're a new Shield Advanced customer and require access to the legacy solution, contact AWS Support."
> — [Automating application layer DDoS mitigation with Shield Advanced](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-automatic-app-layer-response.html)

### shield-udp-reflection-attack

**Claim.** In a UDP reflection attack, an attacker spoofs the source of a request and uses UDP to get a large response from a server, so the extra traffic hits the spoofed, attacked IP address.

**Write it as.** `spoof the source of a request` · `elicit a large response from the server`

**Scope.** DDoS attack types.

> "In UDP reflection attacks, an attacker can spoof the source of a request and use UDP to elicit a large response from the server. The extra network traffic directed towards the spoofed, attacked IP address can slow the targeted server and prevent legitimate end users from accessing needed resources."
> — [Examples of DDoS attacks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/types-of-ddos-attacks.html)

**Checked.** 2026-10-12.

### shield-use-with-waf-multi-layer

**Claim.** AWS Shield defends against large-scale, network-level attacks, and with Shield Advanced you can associate an AWS WAF web ACL with a resource for application layer protection; AWS recommends using both services in tandem for a multi-layered defense.

**Write it as.** `Use both services in tandem` · `for a multi-layered defense strategy`

**Scope.** web application security.

> "While AWS Shield defends against large-scale, network-level attacks, with AWS Shield Advanced, you can associate an AWS WAF web ACL with a resource to provide protection at the application layer. AWS WAF provides more granular protection against application-specific vulnerabilities. Use both services in tandem for a multi-layered defense strategy, safeguarding your applications from a broader range of potential threats across different network layers."
